# Model specification: spi-controller 1.1.0

Master-mode SPI controller as used by PX4 and ArduPilot sensor drivers (full duplex, software or GPIO chip select).

> Athrill reproduces RTOS-level behaviour (docs/device-tree-design.md). SPI uses instant exchange; PX4 (NuttX) and ArduPilot (ChibiOS) drivers work with it, including NuttX waiting for the end-of-transfer interrupt after DMA on STM32H7.

## Features

| Feature | Meaning |
|---|---|
| base | Single-frame full-duplex master transfers. |
| dma | DMA requests for transmit and receive. |
| fifo_threshold | Packet-based status with a programmable FIFO threshold. |
| transfer_size | Counted transfers with an end-of-transfer status. |
| frame_timing | Future (not implemented by any map): frames take frame_size bit times at the baud_divider clock, busy is on while a frame is in flight, transfer_size is enforced. |

## Terms

| Term | Kind | Feature | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| enable | control | base | The controller takes part in transfers; while off, no frame starts. |
| master | control | base | Controller drives the clock. Only master mode is modelled. |
| clock_mode | control | base | CPOL/CPHA. Stored and reported; does not change data in the model. |
| bit_order | control | base | MSB or LSB first. Stored; the byte value exchanged is the frame value. |
| frame_size | control | base | Bits per frame (8 or 16 used by the firmwares). |
| baud_divider | control | base | Clock divider; with the kernel clock it gives the frame time. |
| tx_data | data | base | Writing a frame queues it for transmission. |
| rx_data | data | base | Reading returns the oldest received frame. |
| tx_space | status | base | Another frame can be queued for transmission. |
| rx_available | status | base | At least one received frame (or packet, with fifo_threshold) can be read. |
| busy | status | base | A frame is being shifted. |
| overrun | status | base | A frame was received while the receive storage was full; that frame is lost. |
| overrun_ack | ack | base | Driver action that clears overrun. |
| tx_irq_enable | control | base | tx_space raises the interrupt request. |
| rx_irq_enable | control | base | rx_available raises the interrupt request. |
| error_irq_enable | control | base | overrun raises the interrupt request. |
| irq | event | base | The controller's interrupt line (from the Devicetree interrupts). |
| tx_dma_enable | control | dma | tx_space raises the transmit DMA request. |
| rx_dma_enable | control | dma | rx_available raises the receive DMA request. |
| tx_dma_request | event | dma | Transmit DMA request line (dmas entry named tx). |
| rx_dma_request | event | dma | Receive DMA request line (dmas entry named rx). |
| fifo_threshold | control | fifo_threshold | Frames per packet; rx_available/tx_space refer to whole packets. |
| transfer_size | control | transfer_size | Number of frames in the transfer; 0 = endless. |
| start | control | transfer_size | Starts the transfer (master). |
| end_of_transfer | status | transfer_size | All transfer_size frames have been exchanged. |
| end_of_transfer_ack | ack | transfer_size | Clears end_of_transfer. |
| eot_irq_enable | control | transfer_size | end_of_transfer raises the interrupt request. |

## Behaviour rules

| Rule | Feature | Rule text |
|---|---|---|
| ADV-SPI-B001 | base | When enable is off, writing tx_data starts no frame and busy stays off. |
| ADV-SPI-B002 | base | When enable is on and a frame is written to tx_data, the controller exchanges it with the selected child; the child's frame becomes readable at rx_data and rx_available turns on at the clock of the write (instant exchange). |
| ADV-SPI-B003 | base | Frames are exchanged one at a time in the order written, each at the clock it is written (instant exchange: frame_size and baud_divider are stored but take no time). A timed exchange is the future feature frame_timing. |
| ADV-SPI-B004 | base | busy reads off: under instant exchange no frame is ever in flight when the driver reads the status. |
| ADV-SPI-B005 | base | tx_space is on whenever another frame can be queued; rx_available turns off when the last readable frame is read from rx_data. |
| ADV-SPI-B006 | base | When a frame completes while the receive storage is full, the frame is lost and overrun turns on until overrun_ack. |
| ADV-SPI-B007 | base | irq is raised while (tx_irq_enable and tx_space) or (rx_irq_enable and rx_available) or (error_irq_enable and overrun). |
| ADV-SPI-B008 | dma | rx_dma_request is raised while rx_dma_enable and rx_available; tx_dma_request while tx_dma_enable and tx_space. |
| ADV-SPI-B009 | fifo_threshold | rx_available is on only when at least fifo_threshold frames can be read; tx_space only when fifo_threshold frames can be queued. |
| ADV-SPI-B010 | transfer_size | With transfer_size, end_of_transfer reads on whenever no frame is in flight, which under instant exchange is always; transfer_size and start are stored, and frames written after transfer_size are still exchanged (the count is not enforced; enforcing it belongs to frame_timing). irq is raised while eot_irq_enable and end_of_transfer. |
| ADV-SPI-B011 | base | The controller never selects a child itself; chip select is a GPIO driven by the firmware (Devicetree cs-gpios), and frames go to the child selected at the frame's start. |

**Timing.** Completion clocks and same-clock order follow the timing rules of docs/device-tree-design.md.

**Out of scope.** slave mode, TI mode, CRC calculation, bidirectional (half-duplex) mode, I2S
